display.title: Loss-Free Selective Synaptic Dampening (LFSSD) unlearning method
display.summary: An extension of Selective Synaptic Dampening that replaces Fisher-information parameter importance with the gradient of the squared l2 norm of the model output, so unlearning needs neither the loss nor ground-truth labels.

declarations.statement: To the best of our knowledge, LFSSD is the first retraining-free unlearning method to require only the unlabelled forget samples at forgetting time.

display.title: First retraining-free unlearning requiring only unlabelled forget samples
display.summary: A machine unlearning approach that needs no retraining and no labels, using only unlabelled forget-set inputs at forgetting time and no long-term storage of the retain set.

assessments.attribution: advisory specialist findings from this review run

claim_support.reasoning: The authors define success as similarity to the retrained model. In the ViT subclass rows (sea Df; baby MIA), retrain scores 95.12 and 77.37, while LFSSD scores 20.83 and 1.60. By the authors' own standard, this is over-forgetting. SSD tracks retrain more closely in these same rows. For ViT on Cifar100 lamp, the Df row shows retrain at 0.00, LFSSD at 0.00 and SSD at 36.89. The Dr row shows LFSSD retaining accuracy at SSD's level for both architectures. Class-unlearning rows show LFSSD with Df at 0, matching retrain. In the ViT mushroom subclass row, LFSSD's Df is 31.42, versus 6.68 for SSD and 26.57 for retrain. Results therefore vary by setting.
points: The claim that LFSSD scores are similar to retraining is overstated for subclass unlearning. In several cells LFSSD departs substantially from the retrained model, which is the authors' own target.
On full-class unlearning, the results support the claim that LFSSD is comparable to SSD. In one case (ViT lamp) LFSSD forgets where SSD leaves residual accuracy.
The tables support the claim that LFSSD is competitive with SSD on class unlearning. The introduction's 'equally effective' framing is stronger than some subclass rows show.

significance.reasoning: The paper names storage and label requirements as practical barriers. LFSSD addresses the label barrier while inheriting SSD's one-time computation over D.
points: Removing the label requirement while keeping SSD's one-time computation over D gives a cheap, simple baseline. Researchers working on post-hoc unlearning are likely to adopt it.

originality.reasoning: The authors attribute both components to prior work. The originality therefore lies in transferring the estimator into unlearning, which removes the label requirement. The claim that it 'has not been applied in unlearning' is author-reported and was not verified here. The authors attribute both the estimator and the dampening rule to prior work. What they claim as new is the combination and its use in unlearning. Whether the estimator has truly not been used in unlearning before is author-reported and was not independently verified.
points: The method makes one targeted substitution: it replaces SSD's Fisher-based importance with the output-norm sensitivity estimate from Aljundi et al. (2018). The authors frame this as an extension and credit the source of the importance measure.

The authors present the novelty as transferring an existing importance estimator into unlearning, not as a new estimator. This transfer framing is consistent with the methods section. The originality is therefore incremental: a recombination of SSD with the estimator of Aljundi et al.

assessments.attribution: advisory specialist findings from this review run

claim_support.reasoning: The semi-supervised and copyright-catalogue scenarios are motivations, not experiments. All reported benchmarks use labelled datasets: Cifar and PINS. Equation 3 uses only the output norm, so neither labels nor retraining are needed. Robustness to alpha, however, is shown on a single class (Table 2), and the alpha value differs per task. The authors also acknowledge their reliance on alpha and lambda.
points: The practicality claims ('robust, more practically useful') rest on argument. The label-free scenarios the paper describes are not evaluated.
The retraining-free, label-free property follows directly from the method's construction and is supported. The 'robust' part of the conclusion relies on limited hyperparameter evidence.

significance.reasoning: No grounded, candidate-targeted finding for this axis.

originality.reasoning: The paper cites a zero-shot unlearning work but groups it with retraining-based methods. It never states that work's label requirements. I did not inspect the cited work.
points: The primacy claim is hedged in the introduction but stated without the hedge in the conclusion. The paper does not distinguish its label requirements from those of cited zero-shot unlearning work.
